name: fairy sleep

attributes.attribute: coma-like trance from a fairy taking
kept the tablecloth that wrapped a taken woman
pierced the clothing of one who visited Fairyland
until drawn, the person slept without waking

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy sleep is a folkloric motif of a coma-like trance. A person taken by the fairies might not vanish but lapse into a sleep from which no one could wake them. One victim, a woman from the Burren country in western Clare, lay in such a state. Her rescuer heard the fairies say they still held the tablecloth that had wrapped her. He took back the cloth, and the woman returned to her waking self. A person who came back from Fairyland often found that a small pin had pierced their clothes. The person slept without waking until someone pulled the pin free.

okr.objective: Fairy sleep is a folkloric motif of a coma-like trance.
key_results: A taken person might lapse into a sleep none could wake.
A woman of the Burren was restored when her cloth was reclaimed.
Clothing of a visitor to Fairyland bore a tiny pin.
Until the pin was drawn, the person slept without waking.
